thought: Start where you are. Today, focus on the joy of creating.
prompt: Make one mark you like. A line, a dot, a smear of colour. Then make ten more around it.
milestone: Welcome. You are an artist now. Make your first mark.

thought: Use what you have. Do what you can.
prompt: Gather five things already in your home that can make a mark. Make a small piece using only those.

thought: Making art gives your brain something else to think about. Take a break from life’s worries.
prompt: Set a 15 minute timer. Fill a page with shapes and colour and do not stop until it rings.

thought: Making art consistently puts you around art more often, and looking at art has real benefits too.
prompt: Find a painting you love online or in a book. Spend two minutes looking, then make something with its colours.

thought: You are not a “bad artist.” You’ve just lacked consistency.
prompt: Draw the same simple object three times: fast, slow, and with your other hand.

thought: Tell people about your 100-day goal. Ask them to check in on you. Being accountable helps.
prompt: Tell one person about your 100 days today. Then make a tiny piece just for them.

thought: You’re doing this for yourself. A better you means the people around you are better too.
prompt: Make something that feels like a deep breath.
milestone: One week. Seven days in a row is how habits start.

thought: The cycle: Make Art → Make Mess → Clean Up / Set Up → Make Art → Make Mess…
prompt: Make a mess on purpose. Then clean up and set up for tomorrow.

thought: If someone likes your art, it means they like you. Tell someone you like theirs.
prompt: Make a small piece as a gift. Leave it somewhere, or give it to someone.

thought: What you are doing is important.
prompt: Write one word that matters to you, big, in the middle of the page. Build the art around it.

thought: Make your emotions. Happy art feels happy. Frantic art feels frantic. Dark art feels dark.
prompt: Pick one feeling from today. Make it with colour only, no shapes you can name.

thought: Cleaning up is part of the creative process. Tidy your space and set up for next time.
prompt: Do a quick piece, then spend five minutes making your space ready for tomorrow.

thought: “Creativity is contagious. Pass it on.” – Einstein
prompt: Make something you would want to share. Send a photo of it to one friend.

thought: “Art enables us to find ourselves and lose ourselves at the same time.” – Merton
prompt: Lose yourself: put on one long song and keep your hands moving until it ends.
milestone: Two weeks. You are building something real.

thought: As you work, jot down any important thoughts that pop into your head.
prompt: Keep a notebook beside you. Make art and write down every thought that pops up.

thought: “The more I paint, the more I like everything.” – Renoir
prompt: Paint or draw something ordinary you see every day. Make it feel special.

thought: Art is good for you.
prompt: Make art for 15 minutes before you check your phone.

thought: You become someone when you do something. Do it!
prompt: Finish one small piece today. Done is the goal.

thought: Begin with what you know, and the rest will be revealed to you.
prompt: Start with what you know: draw your hand, your mug, your shoe.

thought: Remember who you are.
prompt: Make a piece about who you were as a kid.

thought: The dots will connect down the road. So do your work.
prompt: Look back at your first nine days. Make a piece that connects two of them.

thought: You can be happy right now.
prompt: Make something happy, even if you are not.

thought: Can you remember the art materials you used and loved as a kid?
prompt: Use a material you loved as a kid: crayons, markers, glue, glitter, play dough.

thought: “The world always seems brighter when you’ve just made something.” – Neil Gaiman
prompt: Make something bright. Put it where you will see it in the morning.

thought: It feels really good to wake up and look at a piece of art you finished the day before, a sense of accomplishment, satisfaction, fulfillment, and purpose.
prompt: Finish something today and leave it out so you see it tomorrow.

checkin.title: Quarterly Check-in
checkin.intro: Twenty-five days in. That is a real habit forming. Take a few minutes to look back before you carry on.
q: How is the art going so far?
Which materials have felt best in your hands?
What has been the hardest part?
Are any patterns or styles starting to emerge?
Have you told anyone you are doing this? What did they say?
Any early ideas for your final project?
checkin.outro: Keep going. The next twenty-five days are where it starts to feel like yours.

thought: On the days it all feels pointless, make one small thing anyway. That’s where the shift quietly begins.
prompt: Lower the bar. Make one small thing, the size of your palm.

thought: There is no wrong way to make art.
prompt: Try a technique you have never tried. Get it wrong on purpose.

thought: Draw your fear and watch it shrink.
prompt: Draw what worries you. Then add something funny to it.

thought: Create like no one is watching.
prompt: Make something you would never show anyone. Enjoy the freedom.

thought: Sharing with others can help them connect with your journey.
prompt: Share something you made this week, online or in person.
milestone: Thirty days. A month of showing up for yourself.

thought: Let your hands do the thinking.
prompt: Close your eyes for the first minute. Let your hands start the piece.

thought: Your imagination can be your worst nightmare or your greatest superpower. Think about what you’re creating, not what might happen later.
prompt: Picture something good happening. Make that.

thought: Trust the process.
prompt: Repeat one shape twenty times. Watch what happens.

thought: Let go of expectations. Just make something.
prompt: Make three quick pieces in 15 minutes. No judging allowed.

thought: An easy way to get inspired: visit an art gallery in person.
prompt: Visit a gallery, a mural or an art book. Make something inspired by one detail.

thought: “Le Chat Noir” was a meeting place for artists.
prompt: Make a piece about a place where you feel like you belong.

thought: Check-in: How is your art workspace? Do you leave your work-in-progress out to look at?
prompt: Tidy your workspace and leave a work in progress out where you can see it.

thought: Create a “travel” bin with all the art supplies you’d need to make art out in the world.
prompt: Pack a small travel art kit. Make something somewhere other than home.

thought: Create with the color of your current mood.
prompt: Choose the colour that matches your mood. Make the whole piece in shades of it.

thought: You’ve made it this far. Keep going!
prompt: Make a piece that celebrates how far you have come.
milestone: Forty days. You have made it this far. Keep going.

thought: Dream of your future.
prompt: Make a picture of a future you want.

thought: ENERGY: adaptability to change.
prompt: Change one thing about your usual way of working: size, tool, time or place.

thought: One day you’ll look back and see how far you’ve come.
prompt: Look back at Day 1. Make a new version of it.

thought: You are creating a habit of healing.
prompt: Make something slow and gentle. Treat it like care.

thought: The world needs more art right now.
prompt: Make something you think the world needs a little more of.

thought: Even five minutes of art counts.
prompt: Five minutes only. Set the timer and stop when it rings.

thought: Slow progress is still progress. A quiet day is not a wasted one.
prompt: Add a small amount to an older piece instead of starting new.

thought: A little art every day rewires the brain.
prompt: Repeat yesterday's piece with one change.

thought: What if the art you make could heal someone else? Unlock them? Make them ask a question? Feel hope?
prompt: Make a piece for someone who is having a hard time.

thought: Okay, have you thought about your final project for Day 100?
prompt: Brainstorm your final project. Make a quick sketch of what Day 100 could look like.

checkin.title: Halfway Point Check-in
checkin.intro: Fifty days. You are halfway, and you have kept showing up. That is the whole secret, and you are already doing it.
q: How do you feel overall, compared to Day 1?
What kind of art are you making most? Which materials keep pulling you back?
What does your final project look like in your head right now?

thought: The harder you work for something, the greater you’ll feel when you achieve it.
prompt: Work a little longer today. Push one piece further than usual.

thought: Daily creativity is self-care.
prompt: Make art as self care: comfy clothes, good music, no pressure.

thought: The more you create, the more you heal.
prompt: Make a piece about something you are letting go of.

thought: Art is a habit, not a talent.
prompt: Practice one thing you find hard for 15 minutes.

thought: Your future self will thank you for creating today.
prompt: Make something your future self would love to find.

thought: There is no rush. Healing and creativity unfold in their own time.
prompt: No rush today. Work slowly on one corner of a piece.

thought: What you create today is one step closer to joy.
prompt: Make a small piece of pure joy.

thought: Keep creating. Keep healing. Keep believing.
prompt: Make a piece using only three colours.

thought: You are not broken. You are becoming.
prompt: Make a piece about becoming. Start in one corner and grow outward.

thought: No one is forcing you to make art. You have the pleasure of doing it!
prompt: Make whatever you want. You get to do this.
milestone: Sixty days. More than half of the journey is behind you.

thought: There are no mistakes, only unexpected surprises.
prompt: Make a mistake early on purpose and build the piece around it.

thought: The process itself is the healing.
prompt: Focus on how it feels to make it, not how it looks.

thought: Some days, just opening this book is the bravest thing you’ll do. That counts.
prompt: Just open your sketchbook. If you make one mark, it counts.

thought: You don’t have to feel hopeful to begin. Make one small mark, and let hope catch up to you.
prompt: Make one mark and let it lead you.

thought: The heaviness you feel today is real, and it is not the whole story. Make something anyway.
prompt: Make something with your darkest colour and your brightest one.

thought: You are still here. That’s not a small thing. Make one quiet mark to prove it.
prompt: Make one quiet mark. That is enough for today.

thought: Healing rarely feels like healing while it’s happening. Trust that it’s working underneath.
prompt: Make something, then turn it upside down and keep going.

thought: On the hardest days, lower the bar. A single line on the page is a victory.
prompt: Draw a single line across the page. That is a victory.

thought: You’re allowed to make something just for you today: no audience, no judgment, no rules.
prompt: Make something nobody will ever see. Just for you.

thought: You don’t have to stop. You can eat later.
prompt: Get lost in it. Work until you forget the time.

thought: The person who started this is braver than you give them credit for.
prompt: Make a self portrait in shapes or colours instead of a face.

thought: Anxiety loosens its grip a little every time your hands focus on something real. Try it now.
prompt: Make art that keeps your hands busy. Fill an area with tiny marks.

thought: You don’t have to fix everything today. You only have to make one thing.
prompt: Make one thing. Only one.

thought: Whatever you’re carrying, set it on the page for a while. Let the paper hold it.
prompt: Put what you are carrying onto the page in colour.

thought: “We are what we repeatedly do.” – Aristotle. You can call yourself an artist now. It’s okay.
prompt: Say it out loud: I am an artist. Then make something to prove it.

checkin.title: Final Quarter Check-in
checkin.intro: Seventy-five days. Most people quit long before here, and you did not. Trust the process now and let the last stretch carry you.
q: How would you describe your style now? What materials have become yours?
Have you finished anything you are proud of?
Your final project: what will it be, and who will you share it with?
checkin.outro: Finishing feels good. Sharing it inspires someone else, and that feels even better.

thought: Your worth was never in question. Let today’s art be a reminder, not a test.
prompt: Make something with no goal at all.

thought: Even now, in the middle of it, something good is taking shape in you.
prompt: Make something hopeful, even if just one corner of it.

thought: Hope is a muscle. Every day you show up here, it grows a little stronger.
prompt: Make something a little bigger or bolder than yesterday.

thought: The world is better with you in it, and better still for the things only you can make.
prompt: Make something only you could make.

thought: Once you start making art, you can keep going. If it feels good, it can become part of who you are.
prompt: Plan how art will stay in your life after Day 100.

thought: You have survived every hard day so far. That’s a perfect record. Keep going.
prompt: Look at your progress tracker. Make something that celebrates your streak.

thought: Be as gentle with yourself as you’d be with someone you love.
prompt: Make something soft and kind.

thought: You are not behind. You are exactly where the next mark begins.
prompt: Pick up wherever you left off. Start with one mark.

thought: Some of your best days are still ahead, waiting on pages you haven’t drawn yet.
prompt: Make a piece about a good day that is still coming.

thought: When the words won’t come, let the colors speak for you.
prompt: Make a piece using colour only. No words, no faces.

thought: Small and steady is still moving forward. And you are moving forward.
prompt: Make something small and steady. Small counts.

thought: If you keep showing up, part of you still believes things can get better. Listen to that part.
prompt: Make a piece about something that is getting better.

thought: You don’t have to believe in yourself all at once. Borrow a little belief from these pages until your own comes back.
prompt: Borrow belief: copy a little of an artist you admire, then make it yours.

thought: Make today’s art a small kindness to your future self.
prompt: Prepare something for tomorrow: a primed page, a laid out palette, a first layer.

thought: Look back through these pages, proof of what you can do, even on the heavy days.
prompt: Lay out your favourite pieces so far. Photograph them together.

thought: Ten days left. How is your final project?
prompt: Work on your final project today.

thought: Whatever you make in these final days, let it be honest. Honest is enough.
prompt: Make something honest. It does not have to be pretty.

thought: You began this when it felt impossible. Look how far that impossible has carried you.
prompt: Remake something from your first week with everything you know now.

thought: The person finishing this book is not the one who started it. You’ve grown.
prompt: Make a piece about who you are becoming.

thought: Be proud of every page, the bright ones and the heavy ones. They’re all you.
prompt: Make one piece you are proud of, bright or heavy.

thought: Almost there. However these days went, you kept showing up for yourself. That matters.
prompt: Almost there. Make something that says thank you to yourself.

thought: This is what hope looks like: doing the small thing again, and again, until it adds up.
prompt: Make the small thing again. Notice how far it has come.

thought: You found your way back to creating. You can find your way back to anything.
prompt: Make something you can come back to after this ends.

thought: One more page, one more reminder that you’re still here, still creating, still becoming.
prompt: Prepare to share your final project tomorrow.

thought: Reflect on how this journey has transformed you. What have you learned? How do you feel now?
prompt: Share your final project. Look back over all 100 days and make one last piece about the journey.

checkin.title: Day 100
checkin.intro: You did it. One hundred days.
q: How has this journey changed you?
What have you learned about yourself?
How do you feel now, compared to Day 1?
How will art stay in your life from here?
checkin.outro: You are an artist. Keep going.
